correctness.rationale: Scaling reduces to width one. For an odd regular n-gon, the maximally separated vertices subtend π−π/n, so its circumradius is R=1/(2 cos b), b=π/(2n). The unit circular arc opposite each vertex is centered there, with half-angle b. The arc flux is 1−R cos u and the squared radius factor is R²+1−2R cos u. The Green integrals, with factors n/2 and n/4 respectively, give the stated A and I by elementary integration. Rotational symmetry forces L²=I/(2A²), so 4πL²=H(b). In `python3 /workspace/checks/independent_01_05.py` (check 5) I independently differentiated H and checked D³H′=b²P, obtained x_8 from formal division of sine by cosine, recomputed the degree-42 rational polynomial and its exact negative-tail bound, and recovered the H series. On 0<b≤π/6 convexity of tangent gives 1≤x≤2√3/π<7/6 and 0<z=b²<1/3. The tangent ODE inductively bounds a_k≤2^(−k); hence 1≤x_8≤x and x−x_8≤(3/1280)z⁹. Termwise differentiation bounds |P_x| by (13+22M)+(16+8M+48M²+4M³)/3+(48M²+24M³+5M⁴)/9<90 at M=7/6. The coefficient and tangent-tail losses are <1/1000 and <1/100 respectively after division by z², against the leading 64/45. Thus H′>0 on the stated continuum, and H(0)=1 gives strict comparison to the disk. The n^(−4) coefficient is π³/180 and n^(−4)−(n+2)^(−4)=8n^(−5)+O(n^(−6)), proving the gap and exact identification at any width. The frozen PASS is recorded, not rerun; the exact replay and analytic bounds do not infer an infinite statement from sampled orders.
